item.title: Jackson Serialization Control: How to Omit Null Fields in JSON Output
item.description:
“Jackson Serialization Control: How to Omit Null Fields in JSON Output”

When serializing Java objects to JSON using the Jackson library, a common requirement is to suppress properties that hold null values. This practice keeps the resulting JSON payload clean and minimizes unnecessary data transfer. Several techniques exist to achieve this, depending on whether you prefer configuration at the ObjectMapper level, class level, or via application properties.

Configuring Serialization Inclusion Globally via ObjectMapper

You can dictate that all subsequent serialization operations should ignore null values by setting the serialization inclusion on the ObjectMapper instance.

item.title: Java Jackson: Deserialize JSON Array to List<MyClass>
item.description:
“Java Jackson: Deserialize JSON Array to List”

When working with Java and JSON data, a common task is converting a JSON array into a structured Java List. The Jackson library provides robust capabilities for this, but there are several ways to achieve this, each with its nuances. This exploration delves into various methods for deserializing a JSON array into a List<MyClass>, offering practical code examples and alternative strategies.

Core Concepts: Jackson and JSON Deserialization

Jackson, a popular Java library, offers high-performance JSON processing. At its heart is the ObjectMapper class, which handles the mapping between JSON and Java objects. Deserializing a JSON array requires telling Jackson the target collection type and the type of objects within that collection.

item.title: Fixing JSON Infinite Recursion with Jackson: A Deep Dive
item.description:
“Fixing JSON Infinite Recursion with Jackson: A Deep Dive”

Encountering a StackOverflowError due to infinite recursion during JSON serialization or deserialization is a common challenge when working with bidirectional relationships in Java, particularly with libraries like Jackson. This occurs when two objects mutually reference each other, leading Jackson’s serializer to endlessly traverse the object graph. This post explores a variety of proven techniques to address and prevent this persistent issue, providing practical code examples and explanations for each.
